definitions.explanation: imposing or collecting fees for a service
paying for items or features within a game or app

examples.japanese: {利用|りよう}{時間|じかん}に{応|おう}じて{課金|かきん}される。
examples.english: You are charged based on usage time.

examples.japanese: {月額|げつがく}{課金|かきん}のサービスだ。
{従量|じゅうりょう}{課金|かきん}{制|せい}で{料金|りょうきん}が{決|き}まる。
examples.english: The fee is determined by usage-based billing.

examples.japanese: ゲームに{課金|かきん}しすぎた。
examples.english: I spent too much on in-app purchases in the game.

examples.japanese: {課金|かきん}しないと{強|つよ}くなれない。
examples.english: You can't get stronger without paying.

examples.japanese: {無課金|むかきん}で{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: I play without spending any money.

notes:
FORMATION:
{課|か} (impose, assign) + {金|きん} (money) → impose money/charges

VERB FORM:
{課金|かきん}する (to charge, to bill; to make in-app purchases)

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {課金|かきん}{制|せい} (fee-based system)
- {従量|じゅうりょう}{課金|かきん} (usage-based billing)
- {月額|げつがく}{課金|かきん} (monthly billing)
- {無課金|むかきん} (free-to-play without paying)
- {廃課金|はいかきん} (excessive in-app spending - slang)
- {微課金|びかきん} (light spending - slang)

MODERN USAGE:
The word has gained a new colloquial meaning in gaming culture, referring specifically to in-app purchases in mobile/online games. "{課金|かきん}する" can mean "to pay real money in a game," often for gacha (loot box) systems or premium items.
